title: devwork · the freshness rendering rule. Every rendered claim carries its date, its anchor, and, when corrected, the version it replaced.
description: Not invented here. This formalises the form already hand-written in /Users/you/work/umbrella/.devwork/connectors/projects/feed-alpha/master.md sections d, e and f — a verified date plus canary rows, and an explicit corrected <date>. The prose is better instrumented than the database, whose scope_entry.last_seen has min = max per project. D-4 in context.md section 4a.

policy.description: freshness as configuration, not as a rule someone remembers. second-brain v2 already ships it in meta as freshness_high_days 7 and freshness_medium_days 30. The band is computed from last_verified_at against this policy at render time and is never typed by hand, so no band field exists on a claim.

last_verified_at.description: srs.md A6: non-null on every row, and every answer renders it. wosy won on the 2026-09-23 battery by showing this date; v2 lost by asserting confidently over nine days of drift.

corrected_at.description: present when this claim replaced an earlier one. master.md writes it literally as corrected 2026-09-10.

superseded_text.description: what the claim said before corrected_at. Required whenever corrected_at is set, because a store carrying both versions with their dates is safer than one carrying a single clean stale version.

anchor.description: what re-verification reads. A claim with no anchor cannot be re-verified, so it decays silently.

canaries.description: the control rows master.md section d already carries: use these when validating new flows. A date with no control is a baseline, not a verification.
